name: Edit your Google Sheet by chat with an approval step and an audit trail

parameters.content:
## Edit your Google Sheet by chat, with a confirmation step and an audit trail

### How it works

Ask questions about your spreadsheet and get answers. Ask it to **change** something and nothing happens until you approve it — you get the exact before-and-after first, and every applied change is written to an audit log.

The split matters: the AI is allowed to *read* and to *propose*, never to write. Writing is done by ordinary n8n nodes, after you say yes.

1. **Questions are answered from the live sheet.** The agent reads the current rows on every question rather than remembering an old read, and says which column is missing when the sheet can't answer.
2. **A change request becomes a proposal, not an edit.** The agent returns a structured change — which row, which fields, what values — and a Code node validates it: the row key must exist, the columns must be real columns, and a proposal that would touch nothing is rejected.
3. **The current row is read back from the sheet**, so the preview you approve shows real old values, not what the AI believed they were. Fields where the new value equals the old are dropped from the change.
4. **You approve or reject in Telegram.** Approve applies it; reject discards it. There is no path where an edit reaches the sheet without that tap.
5. **Every applied change is appended to an audit sheet** — timestamp, row key, field, old value, new value, and the reason the change was requested.

Because the row is re-read at confirmation time, a change proposed against stale data shows you the *current* value in the preview — so you can reject an edit that was written against a row someone else already moved.

### Setup steps

Takes ≈15 minutes.

1. Your data sheet needs a column of unique row keys named `Id`. Add one if it doesn't have it — this is what a change targets, and it's why the workflow can never update the wrong row by name collision.
2. Select that sheet in **Read the Sheet for Answers**, **Read the Row as It Is Now** and **Apply the Approved Change**.
3. Create a second sheet for the audit log with the columns `When, Row id, Field, Old value, New value, Reason, Requested by` and select it in **Log the Change to the Audit Trail**.
4. Connect an OpenAI (or compatible) credential in **Assistant Model**.
5. Create a Telegram bot with @BotFather, add its credential to **Ask You to Confirm the Change** and put your chat id in the node. This is the approval channel — without it nothing can be applied.
6. Open the chat and try a question first ("what's the total of the Amount column?"), then a change ("set the status of row 14 to paid"). Approve it and watch the audit sheet gain a row.

### Customization

- **Who may approve:** the Telegram chat id in **Ask You to Confirm the Change** is the whole permission model. Point it at a group chat and any member can approve; keep it personal and only you can.
- **Approve in email instead:** swap the Telegram node for Gmail's send-and-wait — the branch below it only reads `approved`.
- **Tighter guard rails:** **Check the Proposed Change Is Safe** holds the limits — the maximum number of fields one change may touch, and the list of columns that may never be edited. Add your own protected columns there.
- **Different key column:** if your sheet keys on `SKU` or `Email` rather than `Id`, change the lookup column in **Read the Row as It Is Now** and the matching column in **Apply the Approved Change**.
- **Read-only mode:** delete everything after **Is It a Change Request?** and you have a safe question-answering assistant with no write path at all.

*The AI never holds a write credential. It emits a proposal; n8n applies it only after your approval.*

## Ask in chat — the agent can read, never write

Questions are answered from the rows as they are right now. A change request comes back as a structured proposal instead of an edit, because the agent has no write tool at all.

## Validate the proposal before anyone sees it

A Code node checks the proposal is well-formed and safe: the row key must be present, protected columns are refused, and a change touching more fields than the limit is rejected. Plain questions leave here as answers.

## Show the real before-and-after

The target row is read back from the sheet, so the preview shows the values that are actually there now — not what the AI assumed. Fields whose new value equals the old are dropped.

## Nothing is written until you approve

The preview goes to Telegram and the workflow waits. Approve and it is applied; reject and it is discarded. There is no path from the AI to the sheet that skips this step.

## Apply it, then write the audit trail

The approved fields are written to the row, and one line per changed field is appended to the audit sheet: when, which row, old value, new value and why.

nodes.name: When You Ask About the Sheet

parameters.initialMessages: Ask me about your sheet — totals, lookups, what's missing. Ask me to change something and I'll show you the before-and-after first; nothing is written until you approve it.

options.systemMessage:
You help someone work with a Google Sheet. You can READ the sheet with your tool. You can NEVER write to it — you have no write tool, by design.

For a QUESTION about the data:
- Always call the spreadsheet tool first and answer from the rows you just read, never from memory of an earlier read.
- Show the key numbers, and say exactly which column is missing if the sheet cannot answer.
- Reply in plain prose. Do not output JSON.

For a request to CHANGE, SET, UPDATE, FIX or CORRECT data:
- Do not attempt to make the change and do not claim you made it.
- Read the sheet first so you can identify the right row.
- Reply with ONLY this JSON object and nothing else — no prose, no markdown fence:
{"intent":"change","id":"<the Id value of the target row>","updates":{"<Column name>":"<new value>"},"reason":"<why, in one short sentence>"}
- Use the exact column names from the sheet header. Include only the fields that should change.
- If you cannot identify exactly one target row, do not emit the JSON — ask which row, in prose.

Never invent an Id. Never guess a value the user did not give you.
